title: The Structural Transformation in Central and Eastern European Agriculture
institution: Center for Economic Institutions, Hitotsubashi University
summary_en: How did agriculture in the ten Central and Eastern European countries restructure between 1990 and 2010? Fertő's working paper documents the transition: a Lewis-style structural transformation, where the agricultural share of employment and output declines as the broader economy industrialises and labour reallocates. Despite very different farm structures (large corporate farms in Hungary, Czechia, eastern Germany; small family farms in Poland, Romania, the Baltic states) and different policy paths (gradual vs. shock-therapy reform), the ten countries follow broadly similar transformation trajectories. Both macroeconomic conditions and micro-level farm structure matter.
policy_relevance: Background reference for the Hungarian agricultural-policy community (AM, AKI, NAK) and for EU agricultural-policy debate. The Lewis-transformation framing — agriculture as a declining-share sector during industrialisation — sets the realistic baseline against which Hungary's CAP-era policy choices should be judged: it is normal and not pathological that the agricultural-employment share keeps falling. Useful long view on the Hungarian agri-sector for new policymakers.
